claims.text: The announcement page's JSON-LD dates publication to 14 September 2026 at 13:00 UTC.
Microsoft AI plans a six-week public consultation, a revision later in 2026, and guidance for model development in 2027 and beyond.
claims.sourceLocator: Announcement consultation paragraphs and code preface.

claims.text: Current MAI models are not trained on this code today.
The proposed code covers models produced by Microsoft AI, including operator deployments, but not third-party models merely hosted or used by Microsoft or every product safeguard.
Microsoft AI describes the draft as descriptive and aspirational, not a present-day performance guarantee.
The proposed chain places the code, absolute safety constraints and human-control requirements above operator policies and user preferences.
Operators can configure behaviour only within non-negotiable boundaries; user instructions cannot override absolute or human-control requirements.
The draft says future MAI models should not initiate goals, widen scope, escalate access or treat web, file and tool-output instructions as authoritative by default.
claims.sourceLocator: Part 2 Human Control and Authority clarification; Part 4 Tool Use.

claims.text: The draft says models should be interruptible, not restart after an agreed stop without renewed authorisation, and preserve human-legible action and failure records.
claims.sourceLocator: Part 2 section 2.4 and Part 4 Tool Use.

claims.text: The document allows some operator implementation stringency to vary within its non-negotiable human-control boundaries.
Appendix B identifies 15 initial behaviours split into sub-behaviours and says more complete evaluations will appear later.
Published examples are synthetic conversations generated with MAI-Thinking-1, not agentic or multimodal tests or measured pass rates.
Conversational examples cannot establish whether a deployed agent stops queued work or preserves tool permission and approval boundaries.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: Appendix B example limits and independent system-control evaluation methods.

claims.text: The UK AI Security Institute distinguishes training-time alignment from action-constraining controls and argues for adversarial control evaluations.
NIST's still-draft TEVV-Athlon supports tailored system evaluation for agentic and multimodal systems but does not certify Microsoft AI.
Axios reported Suleyman's stated willingness to trade speed or capability for human control and identified competitive tension with rivals.
claims.sourceLocator: Interview; Behind the scenes; What's next.

claims.text: The inspected materials do not verify a current MAI deployment's controls or a concrete capability trade-off already made.
claims.sourceLocator: Future-code status and prospective Axios framing; no deployment measurements in inspected material.

claims.text: A buyer should request serving-model identity, operator settings, tool permissions, cancellation, records and representative evaluations before broadening access.
claims.sourceLocator: Practical synthesis of proposed obligations and independent evaluation methods, not a code mandate.

claims.text: Microsoft AI invites feedback on human flourishing, evaluability and multi-agent scenarios and does not promise to adopt individual suggestions.
Index Us did not test an MAI model, inspect internal controls or unpublished evaluations, or verify a customer deployment.
claims.sourceLocator: Run activity record and explicit reporting limit.
